audience: operators running coding agents (Claude Code, Kilo, oh-my-pi) on real briefs who need drift caught before it ships
maintainers hot-loading multi-agent coordination into a working repo
authors benchmarking cheap local vs hosted decision lanes on real transcripts
problem: Long agent sessions drift from pinned instructions: constraints vanish after compaction, plans contradict what the user asked, unsupported claims turn into risky tool actions, and the human finds out late. Multi-agent work needs a shared install surface for roles, leases, and proposals, and quality of human-facing output (titles, README) drifts too when no writing contract is pinned.
solution: ACS registers versioned Jev-routing modules: three cheap decision gates (ambiguity, research-needed, tool pin), the jev-court advisor adjudicator, a local Laya benchmark lane with receipts, shared ops capture, and the multi-agent-hotload install surface that wires FULL PCM + FULL CGM 0.5.5 + the coordination runtime without vendoring those helpers.
mechanism: gates pack a tiny constrained package (pins + corrections + proposed action) and ask a cheap judge (local Laya CPU, mock in CI, or third-party hosted lane) for a typed decision
deterministic route policy emits reconfirm_intent / rethink_plan / research_more / dispatch_verifier / escalate / proceed; incomplete or contradictory coverage can never silently proceed
registry.json + POLICY.md define harness/setup/version layout; multi-agent-hotload load order is ACS policy -> FULL PCM -> FULL CGM -> runtime; hotload_check validates pins
decisions append to one shared ops.sqlite and pinned JSON receipts in git; GitHub issues/PRs own progression
